Hi Asha — thanks for the checklist. Drafted a concise MAP (attached) that ties each milestone to an acceptance test and owner. Short summary below; attached file: ClearWave_MAP_v1.xlsx.

Summary (pilot window = 4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (Onboarding): Access + compliance packet delivered — owner: Laura Bennett (SE) — deliverables: SOC2 snapshot, network diagram, KMS approach.
2) Week 1 (Pilot smoke): Hosted-only pilot in US-East — owner: Jordan Blake — deliverables: test harness, 2k synthetic calls, P95 baseline.
3) Week 2 (Load & Eval): Run production-like workload on Dedicated pool candidate if needed — owner: Karthik Iyer — deliverables: latency/cost comparison, quantization profiles.
4) Week 3 (Security signoff): ClearWave security review + short PO/contract step — owner: Chloe Martin — deliverable: procurement checklist satisfied.
5) Week 4 (Go/No-go): Decision gate: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private based on latency SLO, cost delta, and regulatory constraints.

Two quick notes:
- If ClearWave requires on-prem or VPC-only processing for a subset of data, that will shift the pilot timeline by ~2 weeks for environment setup.
- We included fallback policy options in the MAP: start hosted -> canary to dedicated if latency/cost thresholds breached.

Next step: Laura will share SOC2 snapshot and a single-sheet MAP with acceptance checks. Jordan & Karthik — can you confirm owners are ok?

Best,

Thanks team — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions that will determine whether we proceed with hosted-only pilot or insist on dedicated capacity from day one: 

1) In your hosted pilot, will we be able to enforce US-only processing (no model weights or inference outside US)? We need a firm statement for our Legal/Procurement.
2) If we test hosted in US-East and we see a 25% P95 regression under 2k calls vs your dedicated baseline, what is the expected uplift of switching to a dedicated pool (ballpark latency and cost tradeoffs)?

If you can put these two items in a short one-pager, we can move to the procurement review.

Best,
Asha
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@clearwavehealth.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged onramp: hosting + region acceptance ladder (MAP)

Hi Asha — quick answers and next steps (I put numbers below to be explicit):

1) US-only processing: Yes. For the hosted pilot we will pin all routing and compute to US-East or US-West regions, and we will provide an auditable statement that no inference traffic is routed outside the US for your tenant. (We will include this in the procurement packet and the MAP appendix.)

2) Expected uplift moving to Dedicated: based on similar workload profiles we've observed, switching to a Dedicated GPU pool typically reduces P95 by ~20–35% for long-context workloads and ~10–20% for short-context generation due to isolated compute and reservation of batch slots. Cost delta: Dedicated pools start at a predictable monthly commit; for your projected volume (approximate token volume from your 200 qps estimate) we expect a 1.6–2.2x cost per token increase for Dedicated vs shared-hosted, offset by lower tail latency and predictable SLOs. Exact numbers will be in the pilot report.

Next steps: Chloe/Jordan to confirm pilot endpoint and timeline; Chloe will add the two bullets above into a one-page appendix and drop into the Drive by EOB Monday (2026-10-12). If ClearWave confirms US-only requirement, we will record that as a constraint in the MAP and proceed with the hosted US pilot as planned.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
